findings.reason: §2's pass and §6's instrument both target this cohort, so the plan should extend or explicitly reconcile the owner (`classify_parked_source`) rather than maintain a second taxonomy beside it.
findings.text: §6's `_MANIFEST_GENERABILITY_MECHANISMS` defines `attempt_budget_exhausted`, `refusal_cause_not_recorded`, `composition_not_scheduled` and a vocabulary/refusal split, while `graph_ops.py:11405 CAP_PARKED_DISPOSITIONS` already defines a closed, total-by-`classify_parked_source` taxonomy over the same sources with `attempt_budget_exhausted`, `cause_not_recorded`, `vocabulary_gap` and `compose_not_applicable`; the two vocabularies diverge on the lost-cause and not-applicable cases, so a reader querying "why is this source unnamed" gets two answers from two modules

findings.reason: naming the owner would let the plan reuse one tested classifier instead of adding a second, and would have surfaced the `cause_not_recorded`/`refusal_cause_not_recorded` divergence before it landed.
findings.text: the plan's reuse map (`docs/evidence/unbound-source-backlog/export-surface-reuse-map.md`) inventories the export surface but nowhere cites `classify_parked_source` / `CAP_PARKED_DISPOSITIONS`, the existing mechanism that classifies this exact "parked without a name" population, so the §6 taxonomy was designed without the reuse search it needed

findings.reason: at a refusal_families/public_definitions budget of 0 the section must state what it retires or merges, and today it leaves two gates answering the same manifest question.
findings.text: §6 lands a new export gate (`GATE_MANIFEST_GENERABILITY`, `export.py:185`) and a new refusal family (`WaivedSourceDeclarationError`, `export.py:2676`) and states the gate "is the refusal", but it does not name the existing `manifest_source_accounting` gate (`export.py:3075`) it supersedes in role, nor retire it, so the gate inventory grows by one without an accounting

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — `describe_manifest_generability` (`export.py:2496`) hides the disposition→mechanism ladder, the per-mechanism counts and the `generable` fold behind one function over the existing `SourceDispositionRecord` row, so the instrument is deeper than its caller surface.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the §6 mechanism vocabulary forks the parked-source triage taxonomy owned by `imas_codex/standard_names/graph_ops.py:11405`; a second closed vocabulary for "why has this source no name" is a parallel classifier beside the owner.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §6 adds the `manifest_generability` gate constant (`export.py:185`) and the `WaivedSourceDeclarationError` refusal family (`export.py:2676`) without naming, in its own text, what in the gate/refusal inventory it retires or merges, or why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan cites a per-symbol reuse map, but §6 built the mechanism vocabulary `_MANIFEST_GENERABILITY_MECHANISMS` without reconciling the closed, total, already-tested triage taxonomy at `graph_ops.py:11405` (`CAP_PARKED_DISPOSITIONS` / `classify_parked_source`), which answers the same question over the same cohort.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the only remaining executable work §2 proposes is an `sn run` composition pass over the existing `run_sn_pools` (`loop.py:1313`); the plan adds no wrapper layer over it and states the pass reuses the pipeline.
